evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig delayed contact hypersensitivity study
evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction: 1% carbonic acid, methyl phenylmethyl ester in 80% ethanol, dermally applied under occlusion for 6 h, repeated 3 times; challenge: 0.1% and 1% at naive site; species: Hartley guinea pigs (10/sex), 20 animals total; scoring during induction.
evidence.support_text: Based on the result from a range finding study, the dose chosen for induction was 1% and the challenge doses were 0.1 and 1% concentrations in 80% ethanol. Carbonic acid, methyl phenylmethyl ester was dermally applied to 20 (10/sex) Hartley guinea pigs for a total of three 6 h exposures. Fourteen days after the last induction application, the animals were challenged at a naïve site. During the induction all animals (20/20) were noted with erythema; of these animals 11/20 expressed confluent or patchy erythema and 3/20 expressed moderate erythema (RIFM, 1987).

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig delayed contact hypersensitivity study
evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction: 1% carbonic acid, methyl phenylmethyl ester, applied under a Parke-Davis Readi-Bandage covered with a dental dam for 6 h once a week for 3 weeks; challenge: 0.1% and 1% for 24 h; species: Hartley guinea pigs (10/sex); scoring at 24 h and 48 h post-challenge.
evidence.support_text: During a delayed contact hypersensitivity study, 1% carbonic acid, methyl phenylmethyl ester was applied to Hartley guinea pigs (10/sex) for 6 h once a week for 3 weeks. The test material was applied under a Parke-Davis Readi-Bandage covered with a dental dam. Fourteen days after the last induction application, challenge doses of 0.1 and 1% carbonic acid, methyl phenylmethyl ester were applied for 24 h to an untreated site. The sites were scored 24 and 48 h after application of the challenge dose. At 24 h, slight to moderate erythema (grade 1) was observed in 3 and 6 animals administered 0.1 and 1.0%. At 48 h, one animal tested with 1.0% carbonic acid, methyl phenylmethyl ester was noted to have slight to moderate erythema (grade 1). The results were inconclusive (RIFM, 1987).

evidence.support_text: Human serum albumin was incubated in phosphate buffer (pH 8.1) with hex-1-ene-1,3-sultone labeled at position 2 (1b). After dialysis and lyophilization, 13C NMR spectra of the modified protein showed new signals (Figure 2B). After incubation of HSA with 1b, two sets of signals were observed: one at 141.1, 140.0, and 136.9 ppm characteristic of adducts at position 3 (SN reaction) with a conserved sp2 carbon at position 2, and another at 59.6, 45.1, and 44.4 ppm characteristic of carbon-nitrogen bonds through Michael addition at position 2. Extensive dialysis (15 × 5 L) of the protein led to loss of signals at 141.1 and 140.0 ppm, markedly decreased intensity of peaks at 45.1 and 44.4 ppm, and increased intensity of the signal at 59.6 ppm, confirming covalent Michael addition adducts at position 2.

evidence.experimental_conditions: HSA (0.2 µmol) incubated with 12 µmol hex-1-ene-1,3-sultone labeled at position 3 (1a) in phosphate buffer (0.1 M, pH 8.1); incubation followed by dialysis (standard: 15 × 5 L buffer changes) and lyophilization; 13C NMR spectra recorded in H2O/D2O mixture at 400 MHz.
evidence.support_text: Human serum albumin was incubated in phosphate buffer (pH 8.1) with hex-1-ene-1,3-sultone labeled at position 3 (1a). After dialysis and lyophilization, 13C NMR spectra of the modified protein showed new signals (Figure 1B). After incubation of HSA with sultone 1a, two sets of signals were observed: one at 71.4, 68.4, and 66.6 ppm characteristic of adducts from SN substitution at position 3 forming carbon-oxygen bonds, and another at 49.7 and 47.7 ppm characteristic of carbon-nitrogen bonds. When the material was extensively dialyzed (15 × 5 L), the peak at 66.6 ppm and the two small peaks at 49.9 and 47.7 ppm were lost, indicating these were due to noncovalently bound labeled molecules or hydrolysis, while the persistent signals (71.4, 68.4, 49.7 ppm) confirmed covalent protein-sultone adducts.

evidence.support_text: Hex-1-ene-1,3-sultone also reacted with a single lysine residue, initially via an SN reaction at position 3, followed by intramolecular Michael addition at position 2, yielding aziridinium intermediates that were hydrolyzed to an amino alcohol derivative; the same reaction on acetylated HSA indicated the target lysine could be Lys199.
